[spoiler=[b]Expansion:[/b] a (not so) nice trip to the seaside - 339 words (1,000 pixels)]
[i]The idyllic islands of the Amaralo ocean and shamat sea are perfect tourist destinations, but due to the fact that they are unclaimed, it is rather risky to travel there. The expansionist Astaniran government sees an opportunity and seizes it, as it quite literally seizes any unclaimed land in its sight[/i]

[b]7:31am - HST+8 : The northern islands[/b]
The sound of the ocean washing against the shore fills the air around the northern islands, until around 7:31, when the peaceful atmosphere was shattered by an Astaniran warship. A fleet of 217 vessels could be seen on the horizon, rapidly approaching the small islands. The fleet was rather oversized for the task, considering nobody currently claims the islands and it has next to zero inhabitants. Nevertheless, a military got to work quickly surrounding the islands and staking their claim to it. The northern islands, situated in the shamat sea, are now Astanirs sovereign land and nobody can stop them.

[b]7:42am - HST+8 : The southern islands[/b]
Simultaneously, the military also advanced on the islands south of Astanir. This would be a more complex operation, due to the spread out nature of the islands. A task force of 321 vessels was assigned to this job. They split into 3 teams of roughly 100 warships each to swiftly take the islands. Another complication put forward by the southern islands is their inhabitants. Unlike their northern counterparts, these islands are inhabited by aboriginal argossians, who migrated thousands of years ago. The argossians are deeply hated by Astanir as for years they prevented their expansion into the north, but for no longer. As the troops land on the beaches across the several islands, the natives rush out of their crude homes in confusion. 
*BANG* *BANG* *BANG*
Machine gun fire shatters the peaceful silence as the natives ahead drop to the floor. The troops continue to sweep through the island, ripping through anyone that stands in their way. By midday, all of the northern and southern islands are captured.

[b]The Great Islanders Empire has arisen.[/b]
[/spoiler]

[b]Fragmented Elections Due to Corruption in The Polytopian States[/b]

The emergency elections in [b]The Polytopian States[/b], triggered by a corruption scandal of the outgoing government, resulted in an extremely fragmented parliament, with [b]no clear majority.[/b]

[b]The Progressive Liberal Union[/b] surprisingly emerged as the [b]most voted party[/b] (30%), but without a decisive margin. [b]The Social Democratic Party [/b]grew remarkably (22%), while the former ruling party, [b]The Conservative Alternative Party,[/b] was [b]severely punished[/b] (17%).

The rest of the votes were distributed among the [b]Workers' Communist Party[/b] (12%), [b]the Liberal Democratic Party [/b](10%), and the [b]National Unity Party[/b] (9%). This panorama greatly complicates the formation of a [b]stable government[/b], which will likely require a [b]complex coalition.[/b]

[b]Another post, little ramped up because of my now more free time.  [/b]

[spoiler= Gromlash Response Protocol]

The Reichswehrs strike opens with heavy electronic warfare. EK-70 jamming aircraft enter the upper airspace over the northern Nestor Sea approaches, broadcasting across multiple bands. Their signal floods the region, scrambling radar returns and communication links. But Sikirsk's fleet is built for deep-sea war. Ships go dark. Comms switch to directional laser relays and hardened burst-packet transmission, together with [Redacted] encryption. Radar signatures vanish under a layer of decoys, with thousands of EM reflectors and signal drones seeded across the surface. What the Reichswehr sees is a cloud of false fleets, each one reflecting a warship that isn't really there.

REG-3000 anti-radiation missiles arrive next, skimming low. Fired from long-range J-16CJs, they track anything emitting a signal. But the actual emissions are being fed from drones and buoy decoys spread across 60 kilometers. The destroyers only pulse their fire control radars for seconds at a time. In those gaps, Rys-class missiles streak upward, tagging the REGs mid-flight. The REG salvo breaks apart, fooled and hunted in the same stroke.

Below, Sikirsk sonar arrays detect cavitation as submarine-launched Donnerkeil Maritime Strikes rise in wide dispersal from somewhere deep in the Nestor Trough. The missiles arc up toward the sky and reenter at speed, programmed to detonate with EMP bursts on impact. But a month ago, during routine fleet maneuvers, Sikirsk quietly laid a long-range passive sonar web in the area. Now, it pays off.

As launch patterns are triangulated, the fleet disperses fast. EMP-hardening protocols kick in. Reactor systems isolate, antennas retract, sensitive networks go to shielded mode. The Kestrel-class frigates activate their long-range lasers, punching out Donnerkeils in the glide phase. Some get through. One strikes a patrol corvette. Two more detonate in the upper atmosphere, but the damage is shallow. Command and control remains intact.

Then the DF-26Bs arrive.

Launched from converted container-barges deep in the sea zone past the Nestor Shelf, these are carrier killers. Hypersonic, maneuverable, and deadly. They streak in from high arc trajectories. Sikirsk satellites pick them up, and Prometov-500s onboard the lead cruiser prepare to intercept. Each DF-26B begins splitting, MIRVs deploying and decoys scattering. It becomes a sky full of ghosts.

Sikirsks CIWS network engages everything. Bladefang-2s scream as they auto-track incoming targets, using filtered radar, optical lock-ons, and AI-guided prioritization. Liryat-6 energy weapons pulse again and again. One warhead breaks through the chaos and detonates above the fleet, sending a crackling EMP wave down. But the shielding holds. Damage is light.

The stealth cruiser RKS Novastray emerges from thermal shadow under minimal signature a few dozen kilometers east of the formation. It launches a spread of KH-97M anti-asset missiles. The missiles are tuned to hunt signal signatures. They fly low, skipping over the sea surface, and find Reichswehr signal relay buoys, fuel drone hubs, and floating comm towers scattered across the zone. They dont explode big. They just end Reichswehr reach. The enemy's eyes and ears start blinking out one by one.

Meanwhile, deep-sea skimmers from the Voryn Program silently release EM drift pods. These small drifting machines float into Reichswehr jamming zones and begin corrupting the enemys own loops. Now their spoofed data reflects their own ships. Their targeting starts to fold in on itself. Their systems are eating their own noise.

The Reichswehr opened with overwhelming force. Missiles, jamming, decoys, and saturation. They expected confusion, collapse, and a quick kill.

But our fleet adapted.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler= Chyornaya Volna]

The island has fallen. But the fight hasnt.

The last Sikirskian positions in the north were overrun after weeks of bombardment and encirclement. Reichswehr air superiority turned the skies black, and their ground forces swept in under cover of fire, taking what was left after the bombs had done their work. Those defenders who remained fought to the last round or vanished into the smoke.

Now the Reichswehr flies their flags over ash and silence. They claim total control.

Across the ruins, the resistance begins.

Naval units had already landed supply caches and signal kits weeks before the fall. Dispersed cells on the island are now active. Former militia, stranded naval crews, and local fighters blend back into the terrain. They know the land and the towns.

The enemy controls the roads during the day. At night, they lose men. Power stations cut out. Patrols go missing. Bulletholes in fuel tanks. Flags set aflame. 

The hard part of this situation is that the resistance isn't a single entity, they are among the civil populace, civilians join the fight independently and autonomously. All are unsure of who or where the 'enemy' is.

These people are people of Elsyr, protected by their far away brothers, now occupied a imperial and dictatorial Empire.

[/spoiler]
